definition_en: a piece of clothing worn over other clothes outdoors
core_image: 门边的衣钩上挂着一件厚外套，袖口还带着雨滴
scene: 门边的衣钩上挂着一件厚外套，袖口还带着雨滴。He puts on his coat before going out.
sceneCN: 这里 coat 是「外套」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他出门前穿上外套。

senses.title: A warm outer garment
senses.definition: a piece of clothing with sleeves that you wear over other clothes when you go outside
senses.definitionCN: 出门时穿在其他衣服外面、带袖子的衣物
senses.example: He puts on his coat before going out.
senses.why: Old French cote named a long outer garment, and English kept the word for the thing you put on over everything else before stepping outside.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 cote 指长外衣，英语沿用这个词，专指出门时罩在其他衣服外面的那件衣物。

senses.title: A layer of paint or other material
senses.definition: a layer of paint or another substance spread over a surface
senses.definitionCN: 涂在表面上的一层漆或其他材料
senses.example: The wall needs a second coat of paint.
senses.exampleCN: 这面墙还得再刷一层漆。
senses.why: A coat wraps the whole body, so the same word came to name a layer that wraps a surface all over, like paint on a wall.
senses.whyCN: 外套把整个身体裹住，于是这个词也用来指把表面整个裹住的一层东西，比如墙上的漆。

senses.title: To cover something with a layer
senses.definition: to cover something with a thin layer of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 给某物表面裹上薄薄一层东西
senses.example: Coat the fish with flour before frying it.
senses.exampleCN: 煎鱼之前先给鱼裹上一层面粉。
senses.why: The noun sense of a covering layer turned into an action: putting a layer on something is like dressing it in a coat.
senses.whyCN: 名词「一层覆盖物」直接转成动作：给东西加一层，就像替它穿上一件外套。

senses.title: An electronic machine that stores and works with information
senses.definition: an electronic machine that stores data and works with it following a set of instructions
senses.definitionCN: 按指令存储并处理数据的电子机器
senses.example: She writes her story on the computer.
senses.why: Computer is compute plus -er, so the word first named whatever did the computing; once electronic machines took over that work, the name went with them.
senses.whyCN: computer 是 compute 加 -er 构成的，原指做计算的东西；电子机器接手计算之后，这个名字就归了机器。

senses.title: A person who computes (old use)
senses.definition: a person whose job is to do calculations
senses.definitionCN: 以计算为职业的人
senses.example: Long ago, a computer was a person who did sums for a living.
senses.exampleCN: 很久以前，computer 指靠做算术谋生的人。
senses.why: The -er suffix marks the doer, so before machines existed a computer was simply the person who carried out the sums.
senses.whyCN: -er 后缀表示做某事的人，所以在机器出现之前，computer 就是那个负责算数的人。

definition_en: a competition in which people try to win
core_image: 舞台上几个孩子轮流朗诵，评委在台下低头打分
scene: 舞台上几个孩子轮流朗诵，评委在台下低头打分。She enters a singing contest.
sceneCN: 这里 contest 是「比赛」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她报名参加歌唱比赛。

senses.title: A competition with a prize for the winner
senses.definition: an event in which people compete and judges or rules decide who wins
senses.definitionCN: 由评委或规则判定胜负的比拼活动
senses.example: She enters a singing contest.
senses.why: Contest joins con- (together) with a root meaning to witness, so it first pictured people calling each other to witness; a public trial of skill kept that shape.
senses.whyCN: contest 由 con-（一起）加「作证」的词根构成，原本是众人一起对质作证，后来指当众比试高下的活动。

senses.title: To compete for something
senses.definition: to take part in a struggle to win a prize or position
senses.definitionCN: 为奖品或名次参加比拼
senses.example: Three teams contested the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 三支队伍争夺那只奖杯。
senses.why: Turned into a verb, the event word describes what the rivals do inside it: they fight for the same prize.
senses.whyCN: 名词的「比赛」一变成动词，就指参赛者在赛场上做的事：为同一个奖品较量。

senses.title: To argue that something is wrong
senses.definition: to say that a decision or result is not right and try to change it
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个决定或结果不对并设法推翻
senses.example: They contested the referee's decision.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对裁判的判罚提出异议。
senses.why: Two sides calling each other to witness also means standing against each other, and that gave contest the sense of formally disputing a decision.
senses.whyCN: 双方互相传唤作证，也就意味着站到对立面，由此引申出对某个决定正式提出异议。

core_image: 厨房里一口锅冒着热气，有人正用木勺搅动汤
scene: 厨房里一口锅冒着热气，有人正用木勺搅动汤。He cooks dinner for the family.

senses.title: To prepare food by heating it
senses.definition: to make food ready to eat by heating it

senses.why: The noun came first, borrowed from Latin coquus; the verb then named the work that person did, heating food until it is ready.

senses.definitionCN: 做菜的人，尤指以此为业者
senses.example: Her father is a good cook.
senses.why: Old English cōc came straight from Latin coquus, a cook, so the word has named the person in the kitchen longer than it has named the action.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cōc 直接来自拉丁语 coquus「厨师」，所以这个词指厨房里的人，比指做饭这个动作的历史更久。

definition_en: slightly cold in a pleasant way, or calm and fashionable
core_image: 夏天的树荫下有一杯带水珠的冷饮，风吹过来很舒服
scene: 夏天的树荫下有一杯带水珠的冷饮，风吹过来很舒服。The evening air is cool and soft.
sceneCN: 这里 cool 是「凉爽的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是傍晚的空气凉爽柔和。

pos.zh: 形容词：凉爽的、冷静的、酷的

senses.title: Slightly cold in a pleasant way
senses.definition: a little cold in a way that feels comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 凉而不冷、让人觉得舒服
senses.example: The evening air is cool and soft.
senses.why: Old English cōl already meant pleasantly cold rather than freezing, so cool describes a mild, welcome chill.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cōl 本来就表示「凉得舒服」而不是冰冷，所以 cool 指让人欢迎的那种轻微凉意。

senses.title: Calm and not excited or angry
senses.definition: staying calm when others are excited, worried or angry
senses.definitionCN: 在别人激动、着急或生气时保持平静
senses.example: She stayed cool during the test.
senses.why: A cool temperature lowers heat, and the same image was applied to temper: a person who does not heat up stays cool.
senses.whyCN: 凉爽的温度能降下热度，这个画面被用到脾气上：一个人不「发热」，就是冷静。

senses.title: Fashionable and impressive (informal)
senses.definition: fashionable, attractive or impressive, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指时髦、好看、让人佩服
senses.example: He rides a really cool bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他骑一辆很酷的自行车。
senses.why: American slang stretched cool from calm and unbothered to admirable and stylish, the way someone who keeps his head looks impressive.
senses.whyCN: 美国口语把 cool 从「沉着、不慌」扩展到「让人佩服、有型」，因为沉得住气的人看上去就很帅。

senses.title: To make or become less warm
senses.definition: to make something less warm, or to become less warm
senses.definitionCN: 让某物降温，或自身变凉
senses.example: Let the soup cool before you drink it.
senses.why: From the adjective came the verb: if something is cool, then cooling it is the process of bringing it to that state.
senses.whyCN: 从形容词直接生出动词：东西是凉的，让它凉下来就是把它带进这个状态的过程。

scene: 一扇关着的门旁，一个人摊开手，表示自己进不去。He could not open the door.

pos.zh: 情态动词：能、可以，can 的过去式

senses.title: Was able to (past of can)
senses.definition: used as the past form of can to say that someone was able to do something
senses.definitionCN: 作 can 的过去式，表示过去有能力做某事
senses.example: He could not open the door.
senses.why: Could is the past tense of can, so it carries ability into the past: what someone was or was not able to do then.
senses.whyCN: could 是 can 的过去式，把「能」带到过去：某人在当时能或不能做到什么。

senses.title: Used to say something is possible
senses.definition: used to say that something may be true or may happen
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事可能属实或可能发生
senses.example: The answer could be wrong.
senses.why: Ability widened into possibility: if something can happen, it could happen, and the past form softens the claim.
senses.whyCN: 「能力」放宽成「可能」：一件事有能力发生，也就可能发生，用过去式说出来语气更留有余地。

senses.title: Used for a polite request
senses.definition: used to ask someone politely to do something or to allow something
senses.definitionCN: 客气地请人做事或请求允许
senses.example: Could you close the window?
senses.why: Using the past form puts a little distance between speaker and request, which is why could you sounds more polite than can you.
senses.whyCN: 用过去式说请求，会在说话人和请求之间拉开一点距离，所以 could you 比 can you 更客气。

senses.title: Used with have for something that did not happen
senses.definition: used with have and a past participle for something that was possible but was not done
senses.definitionCN: 与 have 加过去分词连用，指本来能做到却没做
senses.example: You could have caught the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 你本来能赶上那班公交的。
senses.why: Could have done points to a past moment when the ability was there but the action never followed, which is why it often carries regret.
senses.whyCN: could have done 指向过去某个时刻：能力在，动作却没发生，所以常带惋惜。

core_image: 一片绿色的田野，远处有几座农舍和一条小路
scene: 一片绿色的田野，远处有几座农舍和一条小路。They walk through the countryside on Sunday.
sceneCN: 这里 countryside 是「乡村」（第 01 个义项）；句意是星期天他们在乡间散步。

senses.title: Land away from towns and cities
senses.definition: the land outside towns and cities, with fields, woods and small villages
senses.definitionCN: 城镇之外、有田野树林和小村庄的地带
senses.example: They walk through the countryside on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 星期天他们在乡间散步。
senses.why: Country once meant the land around a town, and side adds the idea of a stretch of ground, so countryside is the open land beyond the built-up area.
senses.whyCN: country 原指城镇周围的土地，side 加上「一片地方」的意思，countryside 就是建成区之外的那片开阔地。

senses.title: The rural scenery as a view
senses.definition: the fields and villages seen as a landscape, especially when it looks beautiful
senses.definitionCN: 把田野村庄当作一片风景来看，尤指好看的时候
senses.example: The countryside looks golden at sunset.
senses.why: People speak of the countryside the way they speak of a picture, because the fields and hedges outside town are something you stop and look at.
senses.whyCN: 人们说 the countryside 时像在说一幅画，因为城外那些田野和树篱正是让人停下来看的景致。

definition_en: a child of your uncle or aunt
core_image: 两个孩子在院子里一起分一块蛋糕，他们是堂兄妹
scene: 两个孩子在院子里一起分一块蛋糕，他们是堂兄妹。My cousin lives next door.
sceneCN: 这里 cousin 是「堂（表）兄弟姐妹」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我的表妹住在隔壁。

pos.zh: 名词：堂兄弟姐妹、表兄弟姐妹

senses.title: A child of your uncle or aunt
senses.definition: the child of your uncle or aunt
senses.definitionCN: 你叔叔姑姑舅舅姨妈的孩子
senses.example: My cousin lives next door.
senses.why: Latin consobrinus first named the child of a mother's sister; through French the word widened until any child of an aunt or uncle counted as a cousin.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 consobrinus 最初专指母亲姐妹的孩子，经法语进入英语后范围扩大，凡是姑姑舅舅姨妈的孩子都算 cousin。

senses.title: Something closely related to another thing
senses.definition: a thing that is closely related to another, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻有共同来源、彼此相近的事物
senses.example: The two languages are close cousins.
senses.why: Relatives share a common ancestor, so cousin was borrowed for things that also come from one source and stay alike.
senses.whyCN: 亲戚之间有共同的祖先，于是 cousin 被借来指同样出自一个源头、长得很像的事物。

definition_en: a large female farm animal kept for milk
core_image: 一头黑白花的奶牛站在草地上，旁边是一只小牛
scene: 草地上站着一头黑白花的奶牛，旁边是一只小牛。The cow gives milk every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 cow 是「奶牛」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这头奶牛每天早上都产奶。

senses.title: A large female farm animal kept for milk
senses.definition: a large female animal of the cattle family, kept for its milk
senses.definitionCN: 牛科里成年的雌性个体，养来挤奶
senses.example: The cow gives milk every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这头奶牛每天早上都产奶。
senses.why: Old English cū meant an adult female of the cattle family, with bull kept for the male, so the female sense is built into the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cū 专指牛科里成年的雌性，雄性另有 bull 一词，所以「母」这层意思从一开始就在词里。

senses.title: To frighten someone into obeying
senses.definition: to make someone so afraid that they stop resisting
senses.definitionCN: 把人吓到不敢反抗
senses.example: Loud shouts cowed the younger children.
senses.exampleCN: 大声呵斥把年幼的孩子吓住了。
senses.why: This verb came from Old Norse kúga, to force down; it only shares the spelling of the animal and has a separate origin.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词来自古北欧语 kúga「压制」，只是与「牛」拼写相同，来源并不一样。

definition_en: a stick of coloured wax used for drawing
core_image: 桌上散着几支彩色蜡笔，一张画纸上画着太阳和小房子
scene: 桌上散着几支彩色蜡笔，画纸上画着太阳和小房子。The child draws a sun with a red crayon.
sceneCN: 这里 crayon 是「蜡笔」（第 01 个义项）；句意是孩子用红蜡笔画了个太阳。

senses.title: A stick of coloured wax for drawing
senses.definition: a small stick of coloured wax or chalk used for drawing
senses.definitionCN: 画画用的彩色蜡或粉制小棒
senses.example: The child draws a sun with a red crayon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子用红蜡笔画了个太阳。
senses.why: French craie, chalk, plus the small suffix -on gave crayon, a little chalk-like stick; English applied it to the wax colouring stick.
senses.whyCN: 法语 craie「粉笔」加小称后缀 -on 构成 crayon，原指一小截像粉笔的东西，英语用它指裹蜡的彩色画笔。

senses.title: A drawing made with crayons
senses.definition: a picture drawn with crayons
senses.definitionCN: 用蜡笔画成的画
senses.example: That crayon on the wall is her best work.
senses.exampleCN: 墙上那幅蜡笔画是她最好的作品。
senses.why: The name of a drawing tool often passes to the picture made with it, and crayon followed that path from stick to drawing.
senses.whyCN: 画具的名字常常转指用它画成的作品，crayon 也从画笔延伸到了画本身。
